title: Celebrations and the year's holidays
intro: Holidays are a large part of the calendar in Spanish-speaking countries, and the greetings are fixed formulas. Note that feliz goes before the noun: Feliz Navidad, Feliz cumpleaños.

entries.note: See unit 33. el día festivo or el feriado is a public holiday.
Always plural. estar de vacaciones is to be on holiday.

ex.es: Nos vamos de vacaciones en julio.
ex.en: We're going on holiday in July.

entries.note: Capitalised. la Nochebuena is Christmas Eve, and is the bigger celebration of the two.

ex.es: Pasamos la Navidad con mis suegros.
ex.en: We spent Christmas with my in-laws.

entries.note: la Nochevieja or el fin de año is New Year's Eve.
See unit 10. cumplir años is to have a birthday: cumplo treinta.

ex.es: La reunión se celebra en mayo.
ex.en: The meeting is held in May.

entries.note: el pastel in Mexico, la torta further south. In Mexico la torta is a filled bread roll — a real difference.

ex.en: She blew out the candles on the cake.

ex.es: Encendimos velas cuando se fue la luz.
ex.en: We lit candles when the power went out.

ex.es: El barco de vela salió al amanecer.
ex.en: The sailing boat left at dawn.
He pointed at Spain on the globe.

entries.note: desfilar is to parade. la procesión is a religious procession.

ex.es: El desfile pasa por la avenida principal.
ex.en: The parade goes along the main avenue.

entries.note: Also los cohetes for rockets and bangers.
See unit 8. ir a misa is to go to mass.

ex.es: La misa empieza a las siete.

entries.note: la oración is a prayer, and also a grammatical sentence — see unit 23.
Appears constantly in set phrases regardless of belief: gracias a Dios, si Dios quiere, ¡Dios mío!

entries.en: saint, saint's day; Holy Week, Easter
entries.note: Many people celebrate their santo as well as their birthday. Semana Santa is the biggest holiday of the year in much of the region.
See unit 28 and unit 45. envolver is to wrap.

ex.es: Abrió los regalos por la mañana.
ex.en: She opened the presents in the morning.

ex.es: Le llevé un detalle a la anfitriona.
ex.en: I took a small gift for the host.

ex.es: Aquí la costumbre es cenar tarde.
ex.en: Here the custom is to eat late.

entries.note: See unit 33. No celebration in the region happens without both.

ex.es: El baile duró hasta el amanecer.
ex.en: The dancing went on until dawn.

entries.note: disfrutar de algo, or just disfrutar algo. See divertirse in unit 33.
